The reason that a modern compound bow hits so much harder than a longbow or recurve bow of the same poundage:

The only things on a compound bow which is moving more than the littlest bit are the near-massless cams. Almost no stored energy is being transferred back into the frame of the bow in the form of vibration, it’s all being transferred to the arrow. That's one part of it but there is actually a larger effect in the way the cam system of a modern bow inverts the mechanics of an older type of bow.

The full force of a normal bow merely starts the arrow moving; once it is already moving, no more than half the force of the bow acts upon it. The cam system of a modern compound bow allows the strength of the bow to be held against itself.

The archer is holding about a third or a fourth of the strength of the bow at full draw. When the archer releases the arrow, that third starts the arrow moving and then, after the arrow is already moving, the full weight of the bow hits it. In other words, a 60 lb compound bow acts like a recurve bow with sixty pounds at middle draw which would be a much heavier bow.

The fact that little weight is being held at full draw makes the bow easy to shoot accurately. The release device and site system make it extremely accurate.
